skill.computer-use: Operate desktop apps through screenshots and interface controls, checking the result after each action.
skill.domain-check: Review scientific code for unit, coordinate, model and domain-specific errors, and report findings.
skill.large-file: Inspect large datasets with bounded memory, then read only the needed schemas, samples and ranges.
skill.modal-run: Run heavy or GPU jobs on Modal using your account and bring the results back to the workspace.
skill.publication-figures: Create publication-ready figures and tables, checking layout, readability and export formats.
skill.remote-compute: Submit and monitor jobs on SSH servers or Slurm clusters, then retrieve the results.
skill.research-workflow: Organize research from a confirmed objective through planning, method choices, reproducible outputs and evidence checks.
skill.stats-integrity: Check statistical assumptions, preregistration consistency and reproducibility, and flag interpretation risks.
skill.traceability-review: Review whether citations, reported numbers and figures can be traced back to their sources and generating code.

agent.build: Carry out implementation tasks, edit files and run tools to complete the requested work.
agent.plan: Analyze the request and existing project, then prepare an implementation plan before making changes.
agent.general: Handle delegated tasks that require several steps of research, analysis or execution.
agent.explore: Search project files and code to locate implementations and understand how they relate.
agent.reviewer: Review research outputs for traceability, statistics and reproducibility, reporting findings without editing files.
agent.compaction: Condense long conversations while preserving key context so the task can continue.
agent.summary: Summarize the conversation and completed work for later review.
agent.title: Automatically generate a session title from the conversation.

fallback.skill: Provides task-specific instructions for the agent.
fallback.agent: Performs or assists with tasks according to its configuration.

skills.title: Skills & Agents

description.prefix: Loaded live from the OpenCode runtime — the bundled skill packs, everything under
description.suffix: in your workspace, and your own skills in ~/.claude/skills or ~/.agents/skills.

install.placeholder: Paste a SKILL.md, or a URL / description for the agent to turn into one
install.hintConnected: A pasted SKILL.md installs straight away; anything else opens an agent session. Installed skills are available in every workspace.
install.agentPrompt:
The user typed this into the Skills install box:

---
{{input}}
---

Please help them install it patiently: work out which skill they mean (fetch the URL, search for it, or ask them if it is ambiguous), then save it as a skill file at .opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md inside this workspace — never outside it; the app then makes it available in every workspace. The customize-opencode skill documents the format. Finally reply with the installed skill's name.
install.echo:
Please help me install this skill:

{{input}}
install.adoptFailed: The skill was written but could not be moved into your profile, so it will disappear when this session's folder is replaced: {{detail}}
install.hintWorkspace: Installed in the current workspace; available only in this workspace.
install.agentPromptWorkspace:
The user wants to install this skill:

---
{{input}}
---

Confirm its content and source, then save the skill and any required helper files at {{skillsDirectory}}/<name>/SKILL.md inside the current workspace. SKILL.md must have YAML frontmatter with name and description. Keep every file within this workspace; do not write to the user home or another workspace. This installation is available only in the current workspace. Reply with the installed name when complete; report failures accurately without claiming success.

environment.detectionUnavailable: Environment detection runs in the desktop app.
environment.note: OpenCode runs code with whatever is installed here (e.g. Python via its shell tool). uv ships with the app, and Jupyter can be app-managed in Settings → Connectors. Python and R are not bundled — install them or a Science Pack to enable analysis.
